title.en: question forms · present simple vs present continuous

summary.es: question forms · present simple vs present continuous

explanation.es:
El orden de las preguntas

En inglés casi todas las preguntas siguen el mismo esquema. Apréndelo y te servirá para todos los tiempos:

Palabra interrogativaAuxiliarSujetoVerbo…
Wheredoyoulive?
Whatdoesshedoat weekends?
Whyaretheylaughing?
How oftendoyougoto the gym?
Con be y con los modales (can, will…) no hace falta do: Where are you from? Can you swim? Si la pregunta es por el sujeto, tampoco: Who lives here? (no Who does live).

Presente simple y presente continuo

Presente simplePresente continuo
Rutinas, hábitos, hechos y estados permanentesLo que pasa ahora o en esta época (temporal)
I work in a bank.I'm working from home this week.
She usually reads on the train.She's reading a great novel at the moment.
Verbos de estado (like, love, want, need, know, believe, understand, belong, seem) no suelen ir en continuo: ✗ I'm wanting → ✓ I want.
Errores típicos:
  • ✗ Where you live? → ✓ Where do you live?
  • ✗ What does she likes? → ✓ What does she like?
  • ✗ I'm living here since 2020 (se verá con el present perfect) · ✓ I live here / I've lived here since 2020

title.en: past simple: regular and irregular verbs · past questions · time expressions

summary.es: past simple: regular and irregular verbs · past questions · time expressions

explanation.es:
El pasado simple

Para hechos terminados en un momento del pasado: biografías, historias, lo que hiciste ayer. Recuerda: es la misma forma para todas las personas.

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
She moved to Paris in 1990.She didn't move to Rome.When did she move?
He became famous.He didn't become rich.Did he win any awards?

Irregulares frecuentes en biografías

be → was/werebecome → becamebegin → begangrow (up) → grew
leave → leftmeet → metwin → wonwrite → wrote
buy → boughtteach → taughtfall → fellspend → spent

Expresiones de tiempo

in 1985 · in the 1960s · in the 19th century · when she was ten · ten years ago · after university · later · finally · during the war · until 2010
Ortografía de -ed: marry → married, stop → stopped, travel → travelled (RU) / traveled (EE. UU.). Nacer es pasivo: She was born in Lima.
Errores típicos:
  • ✗ When did she moved? → ✓ When did she move?
  • ✗ He died in 1999 ago → ✓ He died in 1999 / He died 25 years ago
  • ✗ She married with a doctor → ✓ She married a doctor / She got married to a doctor

title.en: past continuous: was / were + -ing · when / while

summary.es: past continuous: was / were + -ing · when / while

explanation.es:
El pasado continuo

was / were + -ing. Describe una acción en curso en un momento del pasado: el «decorado» de la historia.

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I was walking home.We weren't watching TV.What were you doing at 8?

Pasado continuo + pasado simple

La acción larga va en continuo; la acción corta que la interrumpe, en pasado simple:

I was having a shower when the phone rang.
While we were walking in the park, it started to rain.
when + pasado simple (acción corta)…when the phone rang.
while + pasado continuo (acción larga)While I was cooking, …
Es como el contraste español estaba duchándome / sonó el teléfono. Pero el inglés no usa el continuo para hábitos del pasado: «de niño jugaba al fútbol» = I played football / I used to play football (✗ I was playing every day).
✗ When I was walking, I was seeing an accident. → ✓ While I was walking, I saw an accident. (ver, oír, saber… no van en continuo).

examples.es: Estaba haciendo la cena cuando llamaste.

title.en: -ed / -ing adjectives · adverbs of manner: quickly, well, hard

summary.es: -ed / -ing adjectives · adverbs of manner: quickly, well, hard

explanation.es:
Adjetivos en -ed y en -ing

-ed: cómo te sientes-ing: lo que lo provoca
I'm bored.The film is boring.
She was surprised.The news was surprising.
We were disappointed.The match was disappointing.
I felt embarrassed.It was an embarrassing moment.
«I'm boring» = soy aburrido (¡no «me aburro»!). Para decir cómo estás, usa -ed: I'm bored, I'm interested, I'm tired.

Adverbios de modo

Dicen cómo se hace algo. Casi siempre adjetivo + -ly y van detrás del verbo (o del objeto):

quick → quicklycareful → carefullyeasy → easilyhappy → happily
irregulares: good → wellfast → fasthard → hardlate → late
She speaks English very well. · Please drive carefully. · He works hard.
Tras be, feel, look, seem, sound, taste va un adjetivo, no un adverbio: You look tired. It sounds good. I feel bad. Y hardly no es «duramente», sino «apenas».

explanation.es:
Comparativos

AdjetivoReglaComparativo

summary.es: superlatives: the -est, the most…, the best, the worst · ever / in the world

explanation.es:
Superlativos

AdjetivoComparativoSuperlativo
talltallerthe tallest
bigbiggerthe biggest
happyhappierthe happiest
beautifulmore beautifulthe most beautiful
good / bad / farbetter / worse / furtherthe best / the worst / the furthest
Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
It's the best film I've ever seen.
That was the worst day of my life.
Detrás del superlativo: in + lugar o grupo (in the world, in my class, in Spain) y of + periodo o cantidad (of my life, of the year, of all). Fíjate en la estructura the best … I've ever … (el mejor … que he … nunca).
✗ the most big → ✓ the biggest · ✗ the more beautiful of the world → ✓ the most beautiful in the world · No olvides the: ✗ It's best restaurant.

title.en: have to / don't have to · must / mustn't · can / can't (permission)

summary.es: have to / don't have to · must / mustn't · can / can't (permission)

explanation.es:
Obligación: have to y must

SignificadoEjemplo
have to / has toobligación (normas, horarios, otros lo imponen)I have to wear a uniform at work.
mustobligación que siente quien habla; carteles y normas escritasI must call my mum. Passengers must show their tickets.
don't / doesn't have tono es necesario (puedes hacerlo si quieres)You don't have to come. It's optional.
mustn'tprohibido, no debesYou mustn't smoke here.
can / can'testá permitido / no está permitidoYou can't park here. You can pay by card.
¡Cuidado! don't have to ≠ mustn't. You don't have to pay = no hace falta pagar (es gratis). You mustn't pay = tienes prohibido pagar.
must no tiene pasado: se usa had to. Yesterday I had to work late. Preguntas: Do you have to wear a tie? (✗ Have you to…?).

title.en: should / shouldn't · What's the matter? · have a + illness

summary.es: should / shouldn't · What's the matter? · have a + illness

explanation.es:
Dar consejos: should / shouldn't

should + forma base = deberías (recomendación). Igual para todas las personas.

You should go to the doctor. · You shouldn't eat so much sugar. · Should I take an aspirin?
Otras formas de aconsejar: Why don't you stay in bed? · If I were you, I'd see a doctor. · It's a good idea to drink water. La palabra advice es incontable: some advice, a piece of advice (✗ an advice, ✗ advices).

Hablar de la salud

What's the matter? / What's wrong?¿Qué te pasa?
I've got a headache / a cold / a temperature.Me duele la cabeza / Estoy resfriado / Tengo fiebre.
I've got a sore throat.Me duele la garganta.
My back hurts. / I've hurt my ankle.Me duele la espalda. / Me he hecho daño en el tobillo.
I feel sick.Estoy mareado / Tengo náuseas.
«Me duele la cabeza» ≠ ✗ Me hurts the head. Usa I've got a headache o My head hurts. Con dolencias se usa a: a cold, a cough, a headache (pero flu sin artículo en RU).

will / won't

title.en: present continuous for future arrangements · invitations: Would you like to…? / Shall we…? / How about…?
title.es: Planes para el fin de semana

summary.es: present continuous for future arrangements · invitations: Would you like to…? / Shall we…? / How about…?

explanation.es:
Presente continuo para planes fijados

Cuando algo ya está organizado (hay hora, sitio, entradas, otra persona implicada), el inglés usa el presente continuo, igual que el español «el sábado ceno con Ana»:

I'm meeting Ana for dinner on Saturday.
What are you doing tonight? — We're going to a concert.
Presente continuogoing towill
plan con fecha/acuerdointencióndecisión en el momento
I'm flying to Rome on Monday.I'm going to visit Rome one day.OK, I'll come with you!

Invitar, aceptar y rechazar

Would you like to come to the cinema?¿Te apetece venir al cine?
Shall we meet at 8?¿Quedamos a las 8?
How about / What about going for a pizza?¿Qué tal si vamos a por una pizza?
Do you fancy a coffee? (RU)¿Te apetece un café?
I'd love to! / That sounds great!¡Me encantaría! / ¡Suena genial!
I'm sorry, I can't. I'm working.Lo siento, no puedo. Trabajo.
Tras How about / What about va -ing: ✗ How about go → ✓ How about going. Tras Would you like va to: ✓ Would you like to come?

title.en: present perfect: have / has + past participle · ever / never · present perfect vs past simple

summary.es: present perfect: have / has + past participle · ever / never · present perfect vs past simple

explanation.es:
El present perfect

have / has + participio. Sirve para hablar de experiencias en tu vida hasta ahora, sin decir cuándo:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I've been to Japan.I haven't tried sushi.Have you ever met a famous person?
She's flown a plane.He's never won anything.Has she ever been to Rome?
Participios irregulares muy frecuentes: be → been, go → gone, see → seen, eat → eaten, do → done, fly → flown, ride → ridden, meet → met, win → won, write → written. Consulta la página de verbos irregulares.

been o gone

She's been to Paris. = Ha estado en París (y ha vuelto).
She's gone to Paris. = Se ha ido a París (y sigue allí).

Present perfect y pasado simple

Primero preguntas por la experiencia (present perfect); en cuanto das detalles (cuándo, dónde, cómo), cambias al pasado simple:

— Have you ever been to London? — Yes, I have. I went there last summer.
— Did you like it? — Yes, it was great.
Con un momento terminado nunca present perfect: ✗ I have been to London last year → ✓ I went to London last year. Fíjate: en España decimos «he estado este año», pero «estuve el año pasado»; el inglés funciona igual con this year / last year.

examples.es: Ha conocido a mucha gente famosa.

examples.es: —¿Has estado en Roma? —Sí, fui en 2019.

title.en: present perfect with just / already / yet · for / since (introduction)

summary.es: present perfect with just / already / yet · for / since (introduction)

explanation.es:
just · already · yet

SignificadoPosiciónEjemplo
justacabar deentre have y el participioI've just finished. (Acabo de terminar.)
alreadyya (antes de lo esperado)entre have y el participioShe's already left.
yettodavía (neg.) / ya (preg.)al finalI haven't paid yet. Have you paid yet?
«Acabo de llegar» no lleva finish: ✓ I've just arrived. En inglés americano también se dice I just arrived (pasado simple).

for y since

El present perfect también expresa algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue. Lo verás más en B1:

I've known her for ten years. (desde hace diez años)
We've lived here since 2015. (desde 2015)
«Vivo aquí desde 2015» ≠ ✗ I live here since 2015 → ✓ I've lived here since 2015. for + periodo (for two hours); since + punto de inicio (since Monday).

title.en: infinitive of purpose: to + verb · by bus / on foot · get on / get off

summary.es: infinitive of purpose: to + verb · by bus / on foot · get on / get off

explanation.es:
Infinitivo de finalidad

Para explicar para qué haces algo, el inglés usa simplemente to + verbo (✗ for to, ✗ for + verbo):

I went to the station to buy a ticket. (para comprar)
She's saving money to travel to Japan.
Why are you learning English? — To get a better job.
✗ I came here for study English → ✓ I came here to study English. Con sustantivos sí va for: I went out for a coffee.

Medios de transporte

by bus / train / car / plane / bikeen autobús, tren…
on foota pie
get on / get off the bussubir al / bajar del autobús
get in / get out of a car / taxisubir al / bajar del coche
take the train / catch the bus / miss the flightcoger el tren / pillar el autobús / perder el vuelo

En el aeropuerto

check in → go through security → wait at the gate → board the plane
A single (ida) / return (ida y vuelta) ticket to Bristol, please.
travel es el verbo; un viaje concreto es a trip o a journey (✗ a travel). luggage es incontable: two bags / some luggage.

title.en: verb + to: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn · verb + -ing: enjoy, like, finish, stop, mind

summary.es: verb + to: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn · verb + -ing: enjoy, like, finish, stop, mind

explanation.es:
Verbo + to + infinitivo

Muchos verbos que miran al futuro (deseos, planes, decisiones) van con to:

want to · need to · decide to · hope to · plan to · learn to · manage to · promise to · offer to · refuse to · would like to
I decided to study medicine. She managed to pass.

Verbo + -ing

enjoy · finish · mind · avoid · imagine · suggest · keep · give up · practise · look forward to
I enjoy cooking. Have you finished eating? Do you mind waiting?
Con like, love, hate, start, begin, continue valen las dos formas casi sin diferencia: I like swimming / I like to swim. Pero would like siempre con to: I'd like to swim. Tras una preposición siempre -ing: I'm good at drawing. Thanks for coming.
stop to ≠ stop -ing: I stopped smoking (dejé de fumar) / I stopped to smoke (paré para fumar). remember / forget to (acordarse / olvidarse de hacer algo) vs remember -ing (recordar haberlo hecho). ✗ I enjoy to read → ✓ I enjoy reading.

title.en: articles: a / an, the, no article · cooking verbs · sequence: first, then, after that, finally

summary.es: articles: a / an, the, no article · cooking verbs · sequence: first, then, after that, finally

explanation.es:
Los artículos

ArtículoCuándoEjemplo
a / analgo que se menciona por primera vez; uno cualquiera; profesionesI've got an onion and a tomato.
thealgo ya mencionado o que ambos conocemos; algo únicoChop the onion. Put it in the oven. the sun
— (sin artículo)plurales e incontables en sentido generalVegetables are good for you. I love chocolate.
El error más típico de los hispanohablantes: poner the al hablar en general. «Me gusta el chocolate» = ✓ I like chocolate (✗ I like the chocolate). «Los perros son leales» = ✓ Dogs are loyal. Tampoco con comidas, deportes, idiomas ni asignaturas: have lunch, play tennis, speak English, study history.
Expresiones fijas sin artículo: at home, at work, at school, go to bed, by car, in hospital (RU). Con artículo: play the guitar, go to the cinema, listen to the radio, watch TV (TV sin the).

Dar instrucciones de una receta

First, chop the onion and the garlic. Then fry them in a little oil. After that, add the tomatoes and stir. Finally, cook for ten minutes.

title.en: defining relative clauses: who, which, that, where · whose

summary.es: defining relative clauses: who, which, that, where · whose

explanation.es:
Oraciones de relativo especificativas

Dan la información necesaria para saber de quién o de qué hablamos:

PronombreParaEjemplo
who / thatpersonasA doctor is someone who helps sick people.
which / thatcosas y animalesThis is the phone which I bought.
wherelugaresThat's the hospital where I was born.
whoseposesión (cuyo)She's the woman whose son won the prize.
Cuando el pronombre es el objeto del verbo, se puede omitir (y es lo más natural): This is the book (that) I told you about. Si es el sujeto, no: The man who lives next door…
Errores típicos:
  • ✗ The man which… → ✓ The man who… (personas)
  • ✗ This is the book that I bought it. → ✓ This is the book that I bought. (no repitas el objeto)
  • ✗ the city where I live in → ✓ the city where I live / the city I live in

title.en: possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs · reflexive pronouns: myself, yourself…

summary.es: possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs · reflexive pronouns: myself, yourself…

explanation.es:
Pronombres posesivos

Sustituyen a posesivo + sustantivo (el mío, la tuya…). No llevan artículo:

AdjetivoPronombreEjemplo
my phonemineThis phone is mine.
your bagyoursIs this charger yours?
his / her laptophis / hersThe blue one is hers.
our / their carours / theirsTheir house is bigger than ours.
✗ It's the mine → ✓ It's mine · ✗ a friend of me → ✓ a friend of mine · Sin apóstrofo: ✗ your's, her's → ✓ yours, hers.

Pronombres reflexivos

I → myselfyou → yourself / yourselveshe → himselfshe → herself
it → itselfwe → ourselvesthey → themselves
I hurt myself. · Enjoy yourselves! · She made the website herself (ella misma, sin ayuda).
Muchos verbos reflexivos del español no lo son en inglés: levantarse = get up, ducharse = have a shower, sentarse = sit down, relajarse = relax, preocuparse = worry, acordarse = remember. ✗ I get up myself.

title.en: first conditional: if + present, will · unless · when vs if

summary.es: first conditional: if + present, will · unless · when vs if

explanation.es:
El primer condicional

Para situaciones reales o probables en el futuro y sus consecuencias:

Condición: if + presenteResultado: will + verbo
If it rains,we'll stay at home.
If you don't hurry,you'll miss the bus.
She won't passif she doesn't study.
¡Nunca will después de if! ✗ If it will rain → ✓ If it rains. Es como en español: «si llueve» (no «si lloverá»).
unless = if … not: I'll go unless it rains (a menos que llueva). when = cuando (seguro que pasará) / if = si (puede que pase): When I get home, I'll call you. If I see Tom, I'll tell him. También se usa presente tras when, as soon as, before, after: ✗ when I will arrive.
If you need help, call me. (imperativo en el resultado)
If you heat ice, it melts. (verdades generales: presente + presente)

title.en: would like / would love · polite requests: Could you…? / Would you mind…? · I'd rather…

summary.es: would like / would love · polite requests: Could you…? / Would you mind…? · I'd rather…

explanation.es:
would like / would love / would prefer

I'd like a table for two, please.Querría una mesa para dos.
I'd love to visit Japan.Me encantaría visitar Japón.
Would you like a drink? — Yes, please. / No, thanks.¿Quieres algo de beber?
I'd rather stay at home. (= I'd prefer to)Prefiero quedarme en casa.
Would you like…? (ofrecer) ≠ Do you like…? (gustos). — Would you like a coffee? — Yes, please (✗ Yes, I like). I'd rather + forma base, sin to: ✗ I'd rather to stay.

Pedir cosas con educación

Más directoMás educado
Can you help me?Could you help me, please?
Can I borrow your pen?Could I borrow your pen?
Open the window.Would you mind opening the window?
A Would you mind…? se responde «no» para aceptar: — Would you mind waiting? — No, not at all. (= no me importa). Para pedir permiso: Do you mind if I sit here?
